# the contributor audit: section normal classification and tangential defect freedom

Full sources read:

- `candidate 53c44db9ae559bfe`, all six sections;
- `candidate 9a1deed5372bf5ee`, Sections 1--7 as available at the time of this audit. Section 8 is an additional pending read.

Both pass in their stated scopes. The geometric/contact-row counterexamples do not carry deepest-source or physical-stress claims.

## Moving sections

Homothety toward any positive parameter anchor gives the sublevel measure bound m|D|t/c. The point need not be an interior center and the section need not have a uniform inball. Layer cake then gives a uniform exponential logarithmic tail. Thus a section defect requires every point in every relevant geometric Hausdorff section limit to have zero limiting parameter. This is stronger than merely locating the eventual measure on zeros.

For the actual bounded finite-plane presentation, each limiting component restricts to the limiting cap plane with either a nonzero tangential gradient, a positive constant, or the zero constant. The first case has a uniform intrinsic strip bound; the second has a positive floor. Finiteness of the plane menu gives uniform logarithmic integrability unless the third case occurs. A component identically zero on the full fiber is excluded by positive interior L. Hence the third case identifies the entire cap plane with a genuine supporting zero plane, whose entire fiber face has continuous codimension at least two. No assertion about the same ambient base tilt at all fibers is inserted.

The proper prelimit truncated-triangle example verifies that unweighted coarea can vanish while logarithmic coarea stays positive. Its normal and coarea factors check, and geometric normalization changes no defect because its bounded logarithm is multiplied by vanishing coarea.

## Convex profile constructions

For the fixed convex profiles A>=H, the lower-body epigraph and finite-min parameter are actual convex/concave objects. The t=x+y change of variables has volume factor t. The inverse primitive separates ordinary inverse density from a nonnegative excess converging to H times the equality-set indicator. The lower-face area factor is delta A sqrt(2+delta^2|grad A|^2); multiplying by its logarithm gives precisely sqrt(2)H on the equality set. All other boundary pieces have uniformly integrable logarithms. These formulas prove the normal-bundle defect rather than infer it from a numerical approximation.

Splitting into fixed active-H cells yields exact tilted rows and uniform original-volume rows. Each limiting row retains an absolutely continuous component throughout its cell, so its mean is interior and the source-core bound is genuine. The disconnected two-plane example has the printed exact moments. A nonnegative PL gap can be decomposed with convex H and A=H+gap, proving the finite-interval support-pattern claim.

For the one-plane interior atom, the flat roof band has width 2/j, height scale 1/j and logarithmic scale j^2. Their product gives boundary mass 2sqrt(2). Off-band integrals are O(delta(1+|log delta|)), not another untracked atom. The raw inverse defect is two and the single row mean is ((1/2+2p)/3,1/12,1/12), uniformly interior. Thus tangential absolute continuity fails even with one affine parameter and one source row.

The fixed finite atomic extension retains a finite H-cell menu. Convex chord replacements majorize H, their slopes stay between its adjacent slopes, and the exterior distance additions produce upward slope jumps. Fixed positive jumps in every inter-band gap bound the off-band logarithmic integrals. Widths delta r_i/(2H(p_i)) produce the stated masses exactly because H is affine near p_i. Every row still retains positive ordinary volume. This is a rigorous finite atomic realization, with no assertion about an arbitrary singular continuous law or a selected bad minimum.

## Consequence for proof design

The section defect is geometrically exceptional in its normal direction, but the surface/volume defect need not be a lower-dimensional uniform or concave-density law. A dimension-reduction argument must use actual cap load, deepestness, and the joint body minimum in addition to these geometric row hypotheses. No recursive OC invocation on the unclassified defect measure is justified.
